notes:
For v0.3.3, trip origins use employed residents (“Ocupado”) from INDEC Census 2022 Redatam at census-radio level. The AMBA
   selection contains 18,018 radios and 7,794,695 employed residents. Formal work destinations use 2022 CEP XXI/SIPA
   establishment records derived from employment registrations. The published worker counts are bands, not exact establishment
   counts; the map assigns capacities of 5, 29.5, 124.5, 349.5 and 500 to the bands 1–9, 10–49, 50–199, 200–499 and 500+,
   respectively. The resulting 4,127,148 formal job capacity is therefore an estimate anchored to official bands. Coordinates
   are rounded to 0.001° in the source. Some geocoded addresses are approximate, and some mobile workers may be recorded at
   central offices.
  
   Each establishment is assigned to its nearest census radio and then an adaptive display cluster; its rounded source
   coordinate is not exported directly. A distance-constrained gravity and transport model balances formal flows against
   employed-resident origins and the estimated workplace capacities. There is no observed origin–destination matrix. The
   remaining 3,667,547 employed residents are represented as local residual employment at residential origins because this
   workplace source does not locate their jobs.
  
   In CABA, official cadastral parcel polygons and the 2022–2024 land-use survey identify active residential parcels. Reported
   floors supply relative weights for a display anchor within each census radio; 3,564 of 3,820 CABA radios receive an anchor.
   Unmatched CABA radios and radios elsewhere retain their census representative point. These parcels do not provide resident
   counts, and the 6,000 exported demand points are display clusters rather than the grain of the published statistics. OSM
   geography and Overture building footprints are used for the map, not to invent resident or job totals. Visible park and
   airport polygons do not add passenger or leisure demand. The residence-placement answer "Spread evenly across each area" is the conservative form category for census-radio representative points outside CABA and parcel-weighted display anchors in CABA; it does not imply that individual residents were uniformly distributed to buildings. — Reviewer refinements (2026-11-05, ahkimn): medium 0.59, the cancun-riviera-maya / merida answers (same pipeline shape: banded establishment records, employed residents per census unit, a gravity model balanced to both totals). Workplace corrected down: workplace_granularity adm5 → adm4 (CEP XXI/SIPA publishes banded headcounts per establishment, not measured counts, and unlike the Mexican DENUE bands no area totals constrain them); workplace_intensity measured_per_unit → fine_types_generic (each capacity is a band midpoint — 5 / 29.5 / 124.5 / 349.5 — with 500+ capped at 500, which understates the largest workplaces; and the 3,667,547 employed residents (~47%) whose jobs the source does not locate — informal, self-employed, domestic and uncovered public employment — are kept as local jobs at their residential origins: cancun spread its informal share across establishments and was held to generic, so this placement can earn no more). Resident corrected up: resident_granularity adm4 → adm5, resident_resolution admin_polygon → mesh_125_or_adm5, resident_intensity uniform → measured_per_unit (INDEC 2022 'Ocupado' counts per census radio — 18,018 radios of ~300 dwellings, the same unit class as a Brazilian setor — merged into 6,000 display points with nothing split below the radio; the 'spread evenly' dropdown was the author's conservative form mapping, as their note says; scored one grain coarser for the ~3:1 merge it is 0.57, still medium). CONFIRMED as filed: workplace_count size_bands, workplace_resolution mesh_125_or_adm5, resident_count employed_residents, od_metric synthetic_measured_marginals (both marginals measured and independent: census employed residents and SIPA establishment bands). AR floor: amba is the first scored AR map and sets the floor.
